newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens ANL spends Dm15mln on freight shipping.
newsitem.headline: Siemens ANL spends Dm15mln on freight shipping.

text.p: Siemens AG Industrial & Building Systems (ANL) said it expected to spend 15 million marks on freight shipping costs in 1997 this year.

Steffen Rudkowsky, Siemens ANL traffic and shipping manager, said that the third-largest Siemens division exported 120,000 tonnes of freight a year with an approximate total value of 650 million marks.
Siemens ANL is a major world supplier of electrotechnical equipment for industry, buildings and transport.

Both shipping costs and freight volumes were likely to be steady this year at 1996 levels although there had been a slight decline in volumes in the first quarter, Rudkowsky told Reuters in an interview.
"We have freight and packaging spending of about 15 million marks a year on average. The hardware transported has a value of about 650 million marks," he said.
Demand for air cargo capacity was growing although some 70-80 percent of ANL freight moved by sea, he added.
"Through the ever-shorter delivery times, we increasingly need air cargo and that now lies by about 15-20 percent," he said.
About 50-60 percent of shipments was transported as containerised freight while the remainder, larger shipments weighing more than 10-15 tonnes, was carried as individual consignments.
Rudkowsky said most freight was transported to the Far East, North America, Europe and CIS states with little demand for South America, Africa or the Middle East.
Projects which would require freight transport in 1997 and 1998 included China, U.S. and Canada, he added.
Air cargo charter demand caused by delivery delays was met through freight forwarders or direct agreements with suppliers such as UK-based Air Foyle.
"The contract is given to the lowest price, the best timing and the best partner," he said.
